exposure: Epidural analgesia with bupivacaine 0.125% and fentanyl 1 mcg/ml
Epidural analgesia with ropivacaine 0.125% and fentanyl 1 mcg/ml
cohort: The study included 44 nulliparous labouring parturients of ASA I & II at term with a singleton, vertex presentation pregnancy, and no obstetric complications.
finding: There was no significant difference between the bupivacaine and ropivacaine groups with fentanyl in terms of analgesic efficacy (duration, onset, sensory/motor block), side effect profile, obstetric, or neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Obstetric outcomes and maternal satisfaction levels were comparable between the two groups receiving different local anaesthetics with fentanyl.
followup_time: Immediate post-birth for neonatal outcomes; study focuses on labour duration.
